title: Tapered grid: reference implementation, benchmark code, and raw measurement logs
description:
Research artifact for Memoization Without Keys: Compact, Out-of-Core Tables for Functions of Sorted Arguments.

tg.hpp is a header-only C++17 memo table for functions of a sorted argument. It stores values only: an entry's address is the lexicographic rank of its sorted argument, computed in O(d) from one shared Pascal table and invertible. A table lives in memory or in a memory-mapped file with a self-describing header, can be filled by any number of threads that each own a range of indices, and answers single, batched and simplex-interpolated lookups.

Contains the library and its tests; every benchmark (in-memory lookups, parallel construction, out-of-core serving, the vector root, an end-to-end maximum-likelihood fit, alpha-entmax); the runner; the raw JSON logs behind every measured number in the paper; and the scripts that regenerate the paper's numbers, tables and figures from those logs. make verify runs the correctness checks and make check-numbers compares the regenerated numbers with the paper's.

Follow-up to Biswas & Regan, Approximation of function evaluation over sequence arguments via specialized data structures, Theoretical Computer Science 607 (2015) 113-123.
